source.title: Northern Whig, 30 April 1927, p. 9 ("Coleraine Rural District"); Ballymoney Free Press and Northern Counties Advertiser, 2 June 1927, p. 3; Derry Journal, 2 May 1930, p. 12 ("Coleraine Rural District Council")
source.publisher: Northern Whig (via the British Newspaper Archive)
source.check: Ballymoney Free Press 2 June 1927 p3 (page image): 'James Mairs' present at the Guardians' meeting of Saturday 28 May 1927; Derry Journal 2 May 1930 p12: the outgoing Drumcroon councillor in 1930 was Mairs.

note: Triennial election of Coleraine rural district (21 divisions, one member each). Nominations were received on 21 April 1927; there was no contest in any division (Belfast News-Letter, 22 April 1927, p. 12). Eighteen members were returned unopposed. No nomination was received for Articlave (previous member James Millen), Bovagh (H. Y. Henderson) or Drumcroon (James Mairs); the previous members continued in office, as the Northern Whig's list (30 April 1927, p. 9) prints, and are recorded from reports of the new council's meetings (meetings gap-fill, 7 Nov 2026). Polled Friday 27 May 1927: 'Polling took place yesterday in the Bellarena division of county Londonderry, the only division in the county where there was a contest' for the county council (Londonderry Sentinel, Saturday 28 May 1927, p. 8), and the Limavady rural contest in Straw 'took place on Friday' (Derry Journal, 30 May 1927, p. 8). No nomination; the previous member, James Mairs, continued in office (deemed re-elected); division from the nominations report itself ('Drumcroon - No nomination (previous member, James Mairs)'). He held the seat to the end of the term: at the 1930 nominations 'Mr. J. Mays [Mairs] ... did not seek re-election' and was succeeded in Drumcroon by Alexander Moore (Derry Journal, 2 May 1930, p. 12). No co-option for Drumcroon was found in 1927-30. Deemed re-elected (no nomination).
